Covered by the 'test' gate (exit 0, uv run pytest -q, which includes this file since testpaths=['tests']).

Only a confirm='0' row is supplied; asserts result == Unavailable(reason=Reason.FETCH_FAILED) and that .value raises AttributeError (Unavailable has no value field per ingest/status.py:53-60). Matches ingest/fetchers/okx.py:37-39.

A 503 response triggers httpx.HTTPStatusError, caught at ingest/fetchers/okx.py:24-25 and converted to Error(reason=FETCH_FAILED, detail contains '503'); test asserts isinstance(Error) and that .value raises AttributeError. This matches the story's own literal AC scope ('an HTTP error returns Error ... and no value'). Note: the separate parsing except-block (IndexError/KeyError/TypeError/ValueError/OverflowError at okx.py:56-60, e.g. malformed JSON or a missing 'data' key) has no dedicated test — only the HTTP-error boundary is exercised — so coverage of 'never raises' is proven for one failure mode, not exhaustively for all of them.

Asserts a candle whose derived close time (open+1 day) is 2026-09-09 while now=2026-09-08T12:00 is rejected as Error with 'future' in detail and no .value attribute; also asserts the accepted case's source_timestamp equals open+1 day and is < now. Matches ingest/fetchers/okx.py:47-53.

Matches the story's own literal AC ('[test: measured_on equals BTC]'), and MEASURED_ON='BTC' is defined at okx.py:12. Caveat: this is a tautological check — MEASURED_ON is a bare module constant never read anywhere else in okx.py and never attached to the returned Result (Ok/Error/Unavailable in ingest/status.py carry no measured/asset field), so nothing at runtime actually 'declares' the measured asset to a caller; the test only proves the constant equals the string it was just assigned.

Calls fetch_btc_daily_close() with no client override, so it goes through the real ENDPOINT (resolved at okx.py:15-17 via ingest.registry.load_registry(), wiring registry.py+status.py+okx.py together) and a live httpx.get to OKX, then independently re-fetches and recomputes the expected closed/newest candle to compare against the result — a genuine assembled-system integration test, not an isolated unit test. No pytest marker exclusion is configured (no addopts/markers in pyproject.toml), so the 'test' gate's uv run pytest -q (exit 0) actually executed this against the live endpoint and passed.

note: All six criteria map 1:1 to named, assertion-real tests that match the story's own literal AC definitions, and both deterministic gates (typecheck, test) exit 0 with no marker exclusion hiding the live-network test. Diff is clean — only the two declared files plus expected .uf/events.ndjson logging, no padding. C3 is proven only for the HTTP-error boundary, not the separate JSON/candle-parsing except-branch (untested, though implemented defensively).
